feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. The candidate is the measured best design, iteration 9 geometry at y 0.06 m, with the controller unchanged. Evidence: iteration 9 and its repeat in iteration 10 both scored 52.985. Moving sensors from y 0.05 to 0.06 m raised oval progress (0.138 to 0.151) and lowered s-bend progress (0.148 to 0.140). Line loss stayed at one per run on oval and s-bend, and steering oscillation stayed between 0.10 and 0.14. Iteration 8 showed that an 8 mm footprint lowers progress, so 12 mm stays. Decision rules: (1) If the s-bend loss stays at its current point and oscillation stays below about 0.2, the offset gain holds and any intermediate offset is a trade-off to weigh, not a clear gain. (2) If oscillation rises above about 0.2, the forward lead is causing lag-driven overshoot, and the offset is at its limit. (3) Because this is the final iteration, no further geometry change can be raced, so these rules are for the Builder's record only.
requested_changes: Keep five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m with y 0.06 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg. Basis: iteration 9 gave the best score (52.985) with oval progress 0.151 against 0.138 at y 0.05 m, and loss stayed at one event per run.

If a future race is run on this geometry, test sensor y 0.055 m with everything else unchanged. Basis: y 0.05 m gave s-bend progress 0.148 (iteration 0) and y 0.06 m gave 0.140 (iteration 9), so an intermediate offset may recover some s-bend progress while keeping part of the oval gain.
If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.2 at y 0.06 m, return sensor y to 0.05 m. Basis: oscillation was 0.07 to 0.14 across iterations 0 to 10, so a jump above 0.2 would show lag-driven overshoot.
